L2 is unsupported by its cited interface: ex-character-lattices states character lattices and the quotient only, not either centre or that isomorphisms preserve centres. The nonisomorphism proof relies on these unlicensed assertions.

A1 and step 2.1 falsely say AC enters only through L3: the cited closed subgroup theorem in L2 assumes AC_ω. Full AC supplies it, so the conclusion follows, but the item inaccurately records its dependency use.

Step 3.1 only proves a homeomorphism onto a closed subgroup. It does not establish that π(G) has the closed-subgroup Lie structure or that π^{-1} is smooth, required for a Lie-group isomorphism by the supplied interface.
Step 3.1 illegally upgrades isomorphisms V_j≅L(λ_j) supplied by classification to the literal equality V=⊕L(λ_j). It proves only V≅⊕L(λ_j), unless identifications are explicitly chosen.

[L2] is not licensed by its cited interfaces: the Lie-group definition and the L^p-density theorem do not state or imply Hausdorffness or existence of a continuous bump separating x,y. The proof’s initial separating f is therefore unsupported.

Step 2.1 is ill-typed: T_{k_n} is an operator, yet f*T_{k_n} is used as a convolution with a function. The cited lemma does not license the asserted integral formula either. The required comparison should be f*p with T_{k_n}f (after defining T_k).

[L3] inaccurately calls (G,K) a symmetric pair “of noncompact type.” The supplied definition additionally requires g₀ to have no nonzero compact ideal, absent from the Statement (e.g. compact semisimple G). Thus its cited metric/curvature interface is not licensed.
Step 1.2 is false: compactness makes a left Haar measure finite, not normalized. Any positive scalar multiple of a Haar probability is a left Haar measure but need not have total mass one.

L2 inaccurately attributes nondegeneracy of the Killing form on all of g to the supplied decomposition and orthogonality interfaces; neither states or licenses global nondegeneracy. Step 1.1 crucially relies on this unsupported assertion.

The proof assumes two maximal tori but never establishes that a compact connected Lie group has any maximal torus. Pairwise conjugacy gives only a vacuous equality if none exist, so it does not license defining a common dimension/rank.

Step 1.1's finite-union proof is invalid: for i≥2 the line u+tv may be contained in H_i (e.g. H_1⊊H_i with u,v∈H_i), so it need not meet H_i in at most one point. Thus its claimed contradiction and nonemptiness inference are unsupported.

[L3] inaccurately restates the Weyl-character-formula interface: it only gives a quotient on regular T extending to the character, not that the restriction is an element of Z[X*(T)] (nor W-invariant). Thus 1.2’s claimed codomain is unsupported.
L3 inaccurately restates its dependency: the supplied theorem asserts only that root spaces are one-dimensional, not that 2γ is never a root. Thus step 4.1 relies on an uncited/unlicensed fact.

Regular values allow empty fibres. Take a point with trivial S^1 action and constant moment map μ=1: 0 is regular and the action on μ⁻¹(0)=∅ is vacuously free/proper, but the claimed dimension is 0−2=-2. F3/F4 do not remedy this.

The definition explicitly assumes \(\mathfrak g\) finite-dimensional, then falsely says it is stated for arbitrary Lie algebras. This is a contradictory hypothesis/scope claim; the displayed definition does not cover infinite-dimensional Lie algebras.

The stated inverse character is ill-typed: \(\chi:T\to S^1\), but it is defined as \(z\mapsto\chi(z)^{-1}\) after \(z\) denotes an element of \(S^1\). It should be \(t\mapsto\chi(t)^{-1}\) for \(t\in T\).

The displayed block solution for \(\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}\) is false and ill-typed: its \((2,1)\) block must be \(n\times1\), though \(w\) is declared \(1\times n\). Correctly, with \(u\) row and \(w\) column, it is \([0\ u\ -w^T;\ w\ a\ b;\ -u^T\ c\ -a^T]\).

It falsely says Ad_{g^{-1}} and Ad^*_g are inverse transposes. If A=Ad_{g^{-1}}, the dual map Ad^*_g has matrix A^T (transpose), whereas A^{-T}=Ad_g^T. Thus the stated smoothness justification contains a false relation.

The Hilbert-space clause is ill-typed: \(\mathcal B(H)\) is not a group under composition (it contains noninvertible operators), so a “group homomorphism \(G\to\mathcal B(H)\)” is undefined. Its codomain must be \(U(H)\) or the invertible operators.

The claimed equivalent formula is false: generally k(x^{-1}y)≠k(y^{-1}x). On the compact Lie group S3, take x=e, a of order 3, f=1_{a}, k=1_{a}; the displayed definition is nonzero while the claimed right-convolution integral is zero.

The cited ideal interface defines only the two-sided ideal generated by a subset; it does not define or establish a left ideal generated by a set. The item inaccurately invokes it for that construction.
False final claim: if V is 1-dimensional, all iterated commutators of its generator vanish, so L(V)=V is 1-dimensional, not infinite-dimensional.

The final sentence wrongly says strictly dominant weights are elements of P. Its own definition only requires positive real coroot pairings; e.g. (1/2)ω₁+… is strictly dominant but generally not in P.

It calls these Hilbert-space representations and states strong continuity is proved “on this page,” but supplies neither a proof nor a cited result for strong continuity. Unitarity and homomorphism alone do not meet the stated Hilbert-space-representation interface.

The cited conjugacy theorem applies only to symmetric pairs of noncompact type, but the definition permits any real semisimple Lie algebra, including compact factors. Thus it does not license the asserted independence of dim a (hence the rank definition) in the stated generality.

The wall definition is wrong: every root hyperplane contains 0, and 0 lies in the boundary of every open chamber (all are cones). Thus it labels every root hyperplane a wall of every chamber, rather than only hyperplanes supporting codimension-one faces.
“Comparisons only occur inside E” is false on h*: for a simple root α, μ=iα−α and λ=iα lie outside E but λ−μ=α∈Q+, so μ≤λ.

The zero semisimple Lie algebra is allowed: then Phi^+=∅ and has no maximal height H. Thus the asserted choice of H and final nilpotence proof fail; the empty-root case (where n^+=0) must be handled separately.

The asserted Iwasawa consequences are justified only by a theorem whose supplied interface assumes the Axiom of Choice, but this definition has no AC hypothesis. That citation therefore does not license the unconditional claims (notably the direct-sum and solvability assertions).

The final claim contradicts the dependency: for E={0}, Phi=emptyset is a finite subset of E\{0} spanning E and satisfies all three axioms vacuously, so the zero vector space does carry a root system under the supplied definition.

The claimed Lie-algebra-level “same object” omits the required no-nonzero-compact-ideal condition. For example (su(2),id) has a Cartan involution but is compact type, not noncompact type under this definition.

It invokes both cited theorems to assert maximal torality and the root-space decomposition, but each theorem assumes the Axiom of Choice while the definition has no AC hypothesis. Thus these assertions are not licensed under its stated hypotheses.

The definition requires Phi to be nonempty, but it then assigns a root datum to every compact connected Lie group. For a torus (including T={e}), the supplied roots interface says Phi(G,T) is empty, so this quadruple is not a reduced compact root datum as defined.

The cited weight-space interface applies only to representations of a complex semisimple Lie algebra with a fixed Cartan subalgebra. Here g_C may be nonsemisimple and t_C need not be Cartan (e.g. a torus), so the claimed “in the sense of” dependency use is invalid.

The proposed equivalence of abstract Satake diagrams is not well-defined: a root system plus a coloured/arrowed base contains no split part \(\mathfrak a_0\) (or restriction map) with which to define the colouring and arrow pairing after a change of base.
The claimed inference B(X,X)≤0 and B(X,X)=B(Y,Y)+B(Z,Z), with B(Y,Y)≤0≤B(Z,Z), “forces” Z=0 is false (e.g. −1=−2+1). Thus α(t₀)⊂t₀′ is not proved by the stated argument.

The definition omits that \(\mathfrak g\) is finite-dimensional. Its cited semisimplicity interface defines semisimple endomorphisms only for finite-dimensional vector spaces, so \(\operatorname{ad}_x\) is otherwise undefined in the supplied sense.

The first remark falsely calls the p-adic integers \(\mathbb Z_p\) a compact connected abelian topological group. \(\mathbb Z_p\) is compact but totally disconnected; this makes the stated example/reasoning mathematically inaccurate.

The abstract-marking claim is false: in A2 with τ swapping the two simple roots, α1+α2 is τ-fixed but there are no τ-fixed simple roots. Its ε-value is unconstrained by the stated rule, so painting does not determine ε.

The well-definedness computation is algebraically wrong: replacing g by gt' gives g(t'tt'^{-1})g^{-1}=gtg^{-1}, not t'gtg^{-1}t'^{-1}. The displayed expression instead corresponds to replacing g by t'g.
The root lattice Q is never defined or supplied by either dependency interface. Thus the claims 2ρ∈Q and ρ∈½Q use an undefined object, making that part of the definition ill-typed.

The displayed definition omits tr(X)=0, so it defines u(p,q), not su(p,q): e.g. iI_m satisfies X*I+IX=0 but has nonzero trace. The later block condition and dimension count instead use su(p,q), leaving the item internally inconsistent.

Step 2.1 falsely states c_j=min(j,a)-max(0,j-b)+1 for every m: it omits the nonnegativity/range condition (and parity). E.g. a=b=0,m=1 gives j=-1/2 and the formula gives 1/2 although w_m=0. Thus its asserted all-weight equality is not proved.

F1 is not licensed by its cited interfaces: the SU(2)/SO(3) item only gives the covering and Lie-algebra isomorphism, while the cross-product definition gives no bracket, adjoint, or coadjoint identification. Thus the key identification is an unsupported dependency restatement.

Step 4.1 is false: sl_1(R)=0 is semisimple (its Killing form is nondegenerate vacuously, also by the cited criterion). Thus n≥2 is not required for semisimplicity or this Cartan-involution construction.

Steps 1.2–1.3 compute centralizers, not normalizers: normalizing a line requires [X,K0]∈RK0 or [X,H]∈RH, not vanishing. The stated calculations therefore do not establish self-normalization (though a further computation could).

L1 and L2 restate the cited GL/SL and U/SU Lie-group examples without their explicit AC_ω hypothesis. The item assumes no AC_ω, so those dependency invocations do not license the asserted real Lie-subalgebra facts as cited.
The statement never assumes n≥1. For n=0, μ⁻¹(0) is empty and CP^{n−1}=CP^{−1} is not the asserted Hopf quotient/manifold, so the example as quantified is false or undefined.
Step 5.1 falsely says both sides have complex dimension dim_C(s). In fact dim_C((s_R)_C)=2 dim_C(s), matching dim_C(s⊕bar{s})=2 dim_C(s); the stated dimension count is wrong.

[L2] inaccurately restates Peter–Weyl: its interface gives normalized matrix coefficients and multiplicities, not that abelian groups have only one-dimensional irreducibles. Step 1.1 relies on this uncited Schur-lemma claim.
No hypothesis k≤n is stated. For k>n, rank(AA*)≤n<k, so μ⁻¹(0) is empty, contradicting the claimed nonempty scaled Stiefel manifold, Grassmannian reduction, and dimension.

Step 4 applies the global theorem without establishing its required global Cartan involution Θ of SL₂(R) and K=G^Θ. The given θ=-transpose is only a Lie-algebra involution; none of the cited steps licenses this missing global hypothesis.

L3 is false: a trivalent diagram with arms 1,1,1 has four vertices (the D4 star), not the three-vertex A3 path. Thus step 2.1’s stated argument for D3=A3 does not follow and misstates the supplied classification interface (D_n arms are 1,1,n−3).

Step 2.1 is false for odd permutations: multiplying a permutation matrix by a diagonal matrix of determinant one leaves its determinant unchanged, so it cannot make it lie in SU(n). One needs a diagonal unitary of determinant (det πσ)^−1.

Step 3 applies L2’s uniqueness for regular Borel probabilities, but steps 1–2 establish only that the pushforward is a translation-invariant Borel probability. Its regularity is neither proved nor cited, so L2 does not license the equality.
[L5] omits the interface’s requirement that Θ fix Z(G) pointwise, and 4.2 never defines or verifies a global Θ (nor G^Θ=SO(n)). Thus L5 cannot license 6.1’s diffeomorphism claim.

L2 inaccurately restates its dependencies: irreducibility plus a base alone does not ensure either signed integral root coordinates or a highest root. The cited results require reduced crystallographic hypotheses, and highest-root existence also requires finiteness.

The item omits c>0 (and restates F1 without it). For c=0 the zero level is {0} with nonfree circle action; for c<0 it is empty. Thus the claimed free Hopf reduction and descent are not licensed by the dependency.

Step 2.1 makes an invalid inference: for one chosen regular H, h_i-h_j=lambda(H) does not imply lambda=f_i-f_j as functionals on a. The all-H hypothesis could prove it, but the stated argument does not, so the exclusion of further roots is unproved.

For the α-string through β=α, β+kα=(k+1)α is nonzero/root at k=-2,-1,0, so p=2,q=0 and p-q=2=α(hα). The item incorrectly uses kα and claims p=q=1.

The displayed cases omit equivalent but nonidentical representations: it uses π≇σ versus π=σ. The cited theorem’s second case requires equality under a fixed identification; for π≅σ with distinct realizations the stated dichotomy gives no value.

Step 1.1 gives a false justification: for the positive root vector E_{12}, one has i=1, contrary to “i≠1.” Thus its stated argument does not establish E_{ij}x_1=0 for all i<j (the correct reason is j≠1).
No hypothesis n≥2 is stated. For n=1, sl₁(C)=0, E₁₁∉sl₁(C), and there is no root/highest root; moreover L1’s conditional simplicity claim is used without establishing its premise.

[L1] inaccurately restates its cited adjoint/highest-root example: that interface asserts the highest vector and weight, but not irreducibility. Thus step 1.2 invokes an unsupported local dependency claim.

L2 inaccurately restates its dependencies: they classify irreducible modules of a complex semisimple Lie algebra, not finite-dimensional representations of SU(2). No cited result supplies the required SU(2)-to-sl_2 correspondence, so L2 (and use of L3) is unsupported.

Step 2.1 is ill-typed: \(\omega_{S^2}\) is on the unit sphere, but \(\xi_{\mathcal O}(\alpha),\eta_{\mathcal O}(\alpha)\in T_\alpha S_r^2\). One must apply the inverse-dilation differential before evaluating the unit-sphere area form.

Step 3.1 is false as written: applying e^{k_0} to w also leaves contributions from every v_k with k>k_0. For w=v_0+v_1, k_0=0 and e^0w is not a multiple of v_0. Thus it does not prove v_0 lies in U(g)w.

Step 2.1 falsely asserts E12∈k0 and E23∈p0. Neither matrix belongs to the real algebra su(2,1): E12 is not skew-Hermitian and E23 is not in its p0. Only their root spaces lie in the complexifications k and p, which the proof does not state.

Fatal level mismatch: with μ(z)=−½∑w_j|z_j|²+c, the stated level μ⁻¹(c) is {0}, not an ellipsoid, and contains no point having only a nonzero j-th coordinate. Thus steps 3–4 and the weighted-projective quotient conclusion do not apply to that level.

Step 1.1 does not establish a homomorphism W(A_n)->S_{n+1}: assigning generators to transpositions requires proving their relations are respected. Step 2.1 is circular/ill-typed, since W(A_n) acts only on the sum-zero subspace, not on all coordinate vectors.
No rank hypothesis is stated. With the library convention 0∈N, n=0 is not excluded, but D_0 has no roots and trivial Weyl group, whereas the claimed order 2^{n-1}n! is 1/2.

[L3] is unsupported by [L1]: that interface establishes only the torus and Weyl action, not that SU(2) has type A1 or that its root character is z↦z². This unlicensed identification is essential to the Jacobian factor.

L4 unconditionally invokes classification by Vogan diagrams, but the cited classification theorem explicitly assumes AC. Neither the facts nor proof assumes AC, so this dependency restatement (and step 3's reliance on it) is not licensed.
Facts misstate the one-dimensional-root-spaces theorem: it does not imply that 2α is not a root. That conclusion follows from the scalar-multiples corollary, not from root-space dimensions.

Step 1.1 miscomputes the su(2) Killing form: if M_a is the matrix of ad_{A_a}, then K(A_a,A_b)=tr(M_aM_b), not 4tr(M_aM_b). With the stated brackets tr(M_aM_b)=-8δ_ab, so its displayed equality is false.

L1 inaccurately restates the tree lemma: it applies only to irreducible root systems with connected Dynkin diagram, whereas a general finite-type Cartan matrix may have a disconnected diagram (e.g. A1×A1).
[L3] inaccurately attributes to the highest-weight classification the claim that all torus weights are characters; its supplied interface states only that highest weights lie in X^*(T).

Step 1.1 crucially asserts that sl_2(C) is semisimple, but no supplied dependency establishes this; the sl_2 interface only defines it and gives its basis/brackets. Thus the alleged witness is not shown to lie in the statement’s quantified class.

Step 1.2 misidentifies s_α: the supplied definition reflects in α^⊥, not in the line Rα. The cited pentagon symmetry therefore does not establish s_α(Φ)=Φ as claimed, so the counterexample proof has a fatal unsupported step.

F1 inaccurately attributes differential/symplectic facts to def-two-dimensional-torus, whose supplied interface only defines T² as a pointed product topological space. Thus dx, dy, ω, ∂x, and the nonzero-period claim are unlicensed.

The title universally asserts that compact groups have infinite-dimensional unitary representations, but the proof establishes this only for S^1. It does not prove the title’s claim for arbitrary compact groups.

[L3] materially misstates its cited interface: it asserts closed subgroups are embedded and gives an exponential Lie-algebra criterion, while the supplied theorem only gives uniqueness/existence of connected immersed subgroups. Steps 1.2 and 3.1 rely on this unlicensed claim.

Step 2.1 misuses L1: its uniqueness is only among measures already invariant under both left and right translations and inversion, but step 1.1 establishes only left invariance of μ_h. Thus L1 does not license μ_h=μ.

Step 1.1 asserts without any supplied or cited dependency that the opposite root space is nonzero, hence that -α is a root. This standard fact is not licensed by the listed interfaces. (Step 2.1 alone would refute the statement.)

[F1] inaccurately restates its cited cotangent-lift proposition: that interface proves the component moment equations but says coadjoint equivariance is verified in a separate companion lemma. No such lemma is cited, so 1.1 and the use of F3 lack an equivariant moment map.

L2 is not licensed by its dependencies: supplied Schur only gives End_G(V) a division ring, not that irreducible unitary S¹-representations are one-dimensional; nor does it supply decomposition of arbitrary finite-dimensional representations. Thus step 1.1 is unsupported.

L3 applies prop-restricted-root-systems-may-be-nonreduced and thm-restricted-root-space-decomposition while omitting their explicit AC hypothesis. Listing def-axiom-of-choice as a dependency does not assume AC; the item never states it.
Step 2.1 reverses the test: step 1 requires dμ=dp, so coordinate p—not −p—works. Since ξ_Q=−∂q, −p(ξ_Q)=p, whereas +p(ξ_Q)=−p. The claimed identification and inference are false.

[F1] is not licensed by its citations: the SU(2)/SO(3) item only states a double cover and Lie-algebra isomorphism, while the cross-product and coadjoint items merely define notions. None establishes the asserted cross-product Lie-algebra and coadjoint-rotation identifications.

L3 misuses L1: L1 only gives dimensions for an already irreducible submodule, not that the submodule generated by an e-killed weight vector is irreducible. This unproved claim underlies the 3+1 decomposition.

The alleged counterexamples are never shown to be semisimple real Lie algebras. The proof only establishes dimension, common complexification, and nonisomorphism; thus it does not verify that its witnesses satisfy the statement’s hypothesis.

[L2] is not licensed by its citations: the supplied interfaces only state a general false claim about real forms and existence of classified root systems, not that su(2)_C=sl_2(C) or that its Dynkin diagram is A1.

L4 is not licensed: the cited weight-space definition gives neither the root-vector shift property nor that U(n^-)v is spanned by weight vectors. Thus 1.2 and the argument that the sum of proper submodules is proper do not follow.

Step 2.1 misuses F4: it makes \(\eta_M(p)\) tangent to the level only for \(\eta\in\mathfrak g_\alpha\), not every \(\eta\in\mathfrak g\). Thus constancy of \(\mu^\xi\) on the level does not prove the claimed vanishing.

Step 4.1 falsely infers R_uH∈V from left-translation invariance. Such subspaces need not be right-invariant (e.g. a fixed-column matrix-coefficient subspace). Thus its Riemann-sum proof of T_k-invariance is invalid; centrality is not used to repair it.

[L3] inaccurately attributes Fubini’s theorem to Haar-invariance and linearity of the Lebesgue integral; neither supplied dependency states or licenses Fubini. Step 1.1 fatally relies on this unsupported assertion.

[L5] falsely says positive roots are exactly all nonzero nonnegative integral combinations of simple roots; the supplied theorem gives only that every positive root has such coordinates, not the converse.

Step 3.1 is invalid: in a direct-sum decomposition of W into irreducibles, v need not lie in any one summand; it may have nonzero components in several. Thus the asserted irreducible summand W_0 “containing v” is unjustified, so [L3] is not applied validly.

Step 2.1 is false: an arbitrary vector in a direct sum of irreducible summands need not lie in any one summand (it may have several nonzero components). Thus no such W0 is licensed, and steps 3–4 do not follow.

Step 2.1 is false: its homomorphism ε sends H to 0, so ε(H−λ(H))=−λ(H), not 0 in general. Thus ρ need not annihilate J, and the claimed injectivity/nonzero v₀ (hence the proof) is unsupported.

Step 3.1 is invalid when q=m-2k<0: the range 0≤j≤q is empty and f_α^q is undefined. Thus it does not establish the needed correspondence for lower h_α-weights (and step 2.1 also wrongly treats all h_α-eigenvectors in T as h-weight vectors).

L2 falsely identifies the character group with Z[X^*(T_p)]; the supplied interface defines it as X^*(T_p). Consequently the statement's “anti-invariant functions” is unqualified and false literally: finite orbit sums cannot be a basis of all functions on T_p.

[L4] is not supplied by its cited dependency: that proposition only identifies character/cocharacter lattices and their pairing; it states no Haar measure or L² orthonormality of torus characters. Step 2.1 therefore lacks its essential premise.
Step 1.1 has a sign error: invariance gives B([e,f],H)=B(e,[f,H])=+α(H)B(e,f), hence [e,f]=B(e,f)H_α, not −B(e,f)H_α. The cited equality B([e,f],H)=B(e,[H,f]) is false.

L1 is not licensed by def-derivation-of-a-lie-algebra: that interface only defines derivations and says ad_x is an inner derivation once its Jacobi-based law is established in a following proposition. No such proposition is cited, so the key derivation step is unsupported.

Step 3.1 invokes nonexistent G-invariant vector fields with arbitrary value X∈p at eK: such a value must be K-fixed. Thus its Koszul computation is invalid, and the later identification of the canonical transport with the Levi-Civita connection is unsupported.
